title: The Signal From Space
text: The Nostromo is not on a heroic expedition. It is an enormous commercial towing vessel, carrying its crew back to Earth after a long haul. Seven people sleep in hypersleep while the ship’s computer, known as Mother, watches over everything. Then Mother intercepts a mysterious transmission and changes the course of their journey. The crew wake expecting to be almost home, but quickly discover they are nowhere near Earth. Their contracts require them to investigate what may be a distress call. Captain Dallas takes charge, while warrant officer Ellen Ripley begins questioning the signal. None of them understands that this detour has already sealed the fate of their ordinary trip. Somewhere below, on a remote and hostile moon, something has been waiting for a visitor.

title: The Alien Warning
text: They land on LV-426, a world of violent weather, barren rock and almost no welcome for human life. Dallas, Kane and Lambert leave the ship to follow the signal toward a gigantic derelict spacecraft. Its architecture looks alive: ribbed passageways, strange curves and walls that seem more biological than mechanical. Deep inside they find the fossil-like remains of a massive alien pilot seated at its controls. Kane presses farther into the structure, eager to discover what lies below. Back aboard the Nostromo, Ripley begins deciphering the broadcast. What everyone assumed was a request for rescue may actually be a warning to stay away. But the landing party has already gone too far to receive it in time. Curiosity, not malice, becomes the first opening the alien needs.

title: The Facehugger
text: Kane descends into a chamber filled with leathery, egg-shaped objects. They seem motionless at first, almost like specimens waiting in storage. He leans close to one and watches its top unfold in four fleshy sections. Before he can react, a spider-like parasite launches upward and strikes his helmet. It burns through the barrier and clamps over his face, wrapping its tail around his neck. Dallas and Lambert carry their unconscious colleague back toward the ship, terrified and desperate to get him treatment. They do not know what the organism is, how it survives, or what it has already done to Kane. The parasite's attack is quick, but its true purpose is not obvious. This is only the first stage of something far worse.

title: Ripley’s Warning Ignored
text: Ripley is the officer at the airlock when the expedition returns with Kane. She makes the hardest decision on the ship: the injured man cannot come inside until quarantine rules are satisfied. Whatever is attached to him could infect or endanger everyone aboard. Dallas argues, Lambert panics, and the situation becomes increasingly desperate. Then science officer Ash breaks the rules by opening the hatch from his side. Kane comes aboard, and every sealed corridor is now potentially compromised. The crew try removing the parasite, but its acidic blood makes even a small incision dangerous. Ash behaves as though studying the organism matters more than protecting his colleagues. At first his actions look like terrible judgment. Later, Ripley learns they are part of a larger betrayal.

title: The Chestburster
text: Eventually the facehugger releases Kane and dies, and Kane appears to recover. For one brief moment, the crew imagine they might resume the trip home. They share a meal, joke nervously and try to restore a sense of normal life. Then Kane begins choking and convulsing on the table. His companions rush to restrain him, but nothing they do can stop what is happening. A small creature violently erupts from his chest, killing him, and darts away before anyone can capture it. The crew has just witnessed the real reason the facehugger attached itself to Kane: he had become a host. The monster is no longer outside in an alien wreck. It is loose inside a ship with a finite number of rooms, vents and hiding places.

title: The Alien Grows
text: The crew split into teams to find the creature before it can threaten anyone else. They expect to be hunting something small, perhaps only a little larger than the animal they saw at dinner. But the organism grows at an impossible rate. Brett goes looking for Jones, the ship's orange cat, and enters a dark machinery space where chains hang from the ceiling and condensation drips through the metal. He hears movement and looks upward. Standing over him is a fully grown Xenomorph: tall, black, biomechanical, with an elongated head and a second set of jaws hidden inside its mouth. Brett barely has time to react. The alien kills him and disappears into the infrastructure of the Nostromo. The remaining crew now realize they are being hunted by a predator perfectly adapted to the ship's darkness.

title: Death in the Ventilation Shafts
text: Captain Dallas volunteers to enter the ventilation system with a flamethrower. The plan is to drive the alien through the narrow shafts toward an airlock, where the crew might finally force it outside. From other parts of the ship, the others follow his movement using a tracking device and relay directions over radio. But the signal becomes unreliable, the passages branch unexpectedly, and every metallic echo sounds like the monster moving closer. Dallas reaches a junction and freezes. He turns his weapon toward the darkness, but the Xenomorph is already there. The ambush happens in an instant. Dallas vanishes, leaving his crew without a captain and without a workable strategy. Now Ripley must take command, and her attention returns to the strange decisions that brought them to this moon in the first place.

title: Special Order 937
text: Ripley accesses Mother and searches for the instructions behind their unexpected diversion. She uncovers Special Order 937, a classified company directive that changes the meaning of the entire mission. The objective is to bring back the alien organism for research. The human crew is explicitly expendable. This means the Nostromo's encounter was not merely a terrible accident. Weyland-Yutani already considered the creature valuable enough to sacrifice its employees. Suddenly Ash's insistence on allowing Kane aboard makes sense. His priorities were never the same as the rest of the crew's. Ripley is trapped between an intelligent alien predator and the corporation that employs her. The monster wants to survive and reproduce. The company wants to own it. Neither cares if she lives.

title: Ash Is an Android
text: When Ripley confronts Ash, the science officer attacks her and attempts to silence her. Parker intervenes, and a struggle leaves Ash horrifically damaged. Instead of blood, a pale synthetic fluid leaks from his body. Wires and machinery are exposed beneath what looked like human skin. Ash is an android, planted aboard the Nostromo to carry out the company's orders. The crew briefly reactivate his severed head, hoping to learn how to kill the alien. Ash offers little useful guidance. He describes the creature with disturbing admiration, viewing it as a perfect organism, unclouded by human conscience. His revelation confirms that the company betrayal began long before the creature reached adulthood. With the captain gone and Ash exposed, Ripley, Parker and Lambert are left to decide how to survive without outside help.

title: The Last Two Deaths
text: Ripley chooses the only plan she can still control: abandon the Nostromo and destroy it. The survivors need supplies before they can take the escape shuttle, so Parker and Lambert go to collect oxygen and equipment. In the red-lit service corridors, the Xenomorph appears. Parker attempts to save Lambert, but the alien kills them both. Ripley hears the violence over the communications system and knows what it means. Every other human aboard the Nostromo is dead. She cannot rescue the crew, contain the organism, or satisfy the company's mission without surrendering her own life. She still has Jones the cat to retrieve, and she has only a short window to reach the escape craft. The story has narrowed to one person against something that has systematically removed everyone else.

title: Destroying the Nostromo
text: Ripley activates the Nostromo's self-destruct sequence. Sirens rise and warning lights flash as she runs through the ship, carrying Jones in a protective box and trying to reach the Narcissus shuttle. Then she sees the alien blocking her route. She backs away and attempts to cancel the countdown, but the system refuses because the deadline has already passed. The ship is going to explode whether she escapes or not. Ripley races through the final corridors and launches the shuttle with seconds to spare. Behind her, the enormous Nostromo disintegrates in a blinding blast. The ordeal seems over. She has escaped the corporate mission and the predator that wiped out her crew. But in the dim interior of the small shuttle, there is a shape she has not noticed.

title: The Last Survivor
text: Ripley prepares for hypersleep, believing she is finally alone with Jones. Then a dark mechanical shape shifts among the shuttle's pipes. The alien has somehow concealed itself aboard the Narcissus. There is no other room to run to and no armed team to help. Ripley keeps her composure, puts on a spacesuit and carefully opens the shuttle's airlock. When the monster moves, she triggers decompression, forcing it out into space. Even then the creature clings to the exterior, so Ripley fires the shuttle engines to blast it away for good. Only after that final struggle can she record her last message and enter hypersleep beside Jones. The Nostromo's entire human crew is gone except for Ellen Ripley. She survived the alien, but the company that wanted it is still out there.
